artworks.title: Playing Cards
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of soldiers in a relaxed setting. The scene shows several figures in various poses, some seated on the ground while others are standing or leaning against a structure. The style uses simple pencil lines to portray the figures, with some having visible facial features and distinct hats. The figures appear to be engaged in an informal gathering, possibly playing cards, as suggested by the positions of their hands. The image captures a moment of respite among uniforms and military attire, conveying a sense of camaraderie and pause amidst their surroundings.

artworks.title: Sutler's Tent, 3rd Pennsylvania Cavalry [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite and charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of military figures in a camp scene. The image shows individuals gathered under a makeshift shelter supported by wooden poles and intersecting branches. The scene depicts a moment of rest or casual interaction within a military camp, based on the uniforms and hats worn by the figures. The drawing is done in a sketch style, offering only an outline and minimal details. The setting appears rustic and temporary with the structure of the shelter and the positioning of the figures, some of whom seem to be leaning or sitting on makeshift benches or tables.

artworks.title: Thanksgiving in Camp [verso]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch with abstract elements. The drawing features rough outlines of figures with abstract landscapes or gardening elements. It is done in pencil with lines and shading. Unclear text and shapes are also part of the composition, contributing to its abstract quality.

artworks.title: Carrying the Wounded
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image features a pencil sketch of a scene set in an open field. The viewpoint is from a moderate distance, looking at a group of three figures standing close to us. In front of them are tree stumps scattered across the ground, suggesting a recently cleared area. The horizon line is somewhat indistinct but can be imagined to run across the middle of the image, with a cluster of trees beyond the figures. The trees break the open space above them. The drawing is executed with light, sketchy pencil lines, providing a sense of spontaneity and immediacy. The overall color palette is monochromatic, using muted tones of pencil on paper to create a subdued visual effect.

artworks.title: Prisoners of War
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image shows three full-bodied figures standing together in conversation. Each person is positioned standing up, with one slightly leaning to the left. The figures have indistinct facial features, and their hair is covered by wide-brimmed hats. They are dressed in simple clothing, consisting of long coats and trousers. One figure appears to have a bandaged leg. The clothing is drawn with lines indicating texture and folds. Each person has a bag slung over their shoulder. There are also two smaller sketches of individuals, one enclosed in a circular design above the main figures. The background is lightly sketched with lines suggesting a row of plants or trees.

artworks.title: Grant and Lincoln at City Point, Virginia [recto]
artworks.medium: charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The sketch shows four individuals standing closely together in an undefined location. The figures are depicted from the back, wearing suits with long overcoats and top hats. Their facial features and hair are not detailed due to the sketchy nature of the image. There are no visible jewelry or objects being held by the individuals. The background is minimal, with faint lines hinting at an outdoor setting and other vague elements nearby.

artworks.title: Study for "Army Boots" [verso]
artworks.medium: graphite and white chalk on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image shows five individuals in a crowded space. Two individuals in the foreground are lying on their stomachs, with one resting his chin on his hands and the other peering over the edge of a platform or bunk. They have bright eyes and short, curly hair, and wear loose-fitting clothing. The other individuals' faces are partially visible in the lower part of the image, indicating they are lying or reclining. The background is simplistic with vertical lines and shading, suggesting an indoor environment. The drawing is done in pencil on paper with visible pencil strokes.

artworks.title: From Alexandria to Ship Point [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: This is a drawing of several individuals gathered in a confined interior space. The drawing features a number of figures, some seated and others lounging on the floor. The setting is cramped with objects hanging from the ceiling or walls. The figures are outlined with loose, flowing lines. The space appears structured with visible overhead beams, and there are a variety of items such as swords or tools suspended around them. The drawing uses a monochromatic color scheme, relying on line work to convey the forms and the environment.

artworks.title: Soldiers and Cannon [verso]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The sketch displays a landscape with minimalistic line work. The horizon is in the middle of the paper, dividing the land and the sky. Trees and a cannon are drawn along the horizon. Figures, possibly soldiers, are depicted in various poses. The background shows faint indications of trees and structures. The pencil work is light and delicate, giving the drawing a monochromatic and soft appearance due to the graphite on the textured paper.

artworks.title: A Shell in the Trenches before Richmond [recto]
artworks.medium: charcoal and graphite with watercolor on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image depicts a battlefield scene with figures in trenches. The inscription reads "A shell in the trenches before Richmond." The drawing shows chaotic movement and intensity, sketched with swift lines on brown paper. It captures immediacy and turmoil, possibly representing smoke, dirt, and movement related to an explosion or shell impact. The tone is tense and hectic, with urgency and action conveyed through rough pencil marks.

artworks.title: Two Soldiers Resting [verso]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: This drawing depicts two seated individuals. One person is fully covered with a draped cloth, obscuring their head and body. They are hunched forward in a sitting position. The other person is seated in a relaxed pose, wearing a uniform or coat with visible buttons. Their face is partially visible, and they wear a hat. The surrounding area includes rough sketches of fabric hangings and a box with the number "61" on it. The background is minimally detailed with light sketch lines.

artworks.title: Advance of the Skirmish Line
artworks.medium: graphite and black and white chalk on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image shows an unfinished sketch viewed from a slightly elevated perspective, portraying a scene with trees, brush lines, two figures in uniforms in a wooded area with stumps and a fallen tree trunk. The sketch features loose pencil or charcoal strokes in a monochromatic color palette, creating a rough and spontaneous quality reminiscent of a quick field sketch.

artworks.title: Line-ups and Trenches [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image shows a sketch of a camp viewed from a slightly elevated perspective. The horizon line is high in the composition, with distant clusters of soldiers and encampments depicted with minimalist lines. Closer to the viewer are rough pencil sketches of figures, possibly soldiers, in various poses. Beyond them, the landscape slopes upwards towards tents and military structures, with faint indications of foliage. The artist uses a loose, casual technique with light pencil strokes, creating a sense of immediacy. The color palette is neutral and monochrome, with the paper's light brown tone complementing the graphite pencil marks.

artworks.title: Supply Train and Mules [verso]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Dr. Edmund Louis Gray Zalinski, II
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch on light textured paper of horse-drawn covered wagons. The scene shows a series of wagons extending into the distance. A horse is on the left, and the largest wagon is in the center with detailed wheels and a visible cover. Smaller covered wagons and figures suggest a convoy, receding into the upper right. The sketch uses delicate pencil strokes for a sense of movement. The palette is monochromatic, with soft pencil gray tones against the tan paper.

artworks.title: Italian Landscape with a Watermill
artworks.medium: brown wash over graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with a watermill in the center, water flowing from its wheel. A man is walking on a path to the right. A stream winds through the scene towards hills and a building in the distance. Trees are present throughout, adding texture. The color palette is sepia, emphasizing light and shadow. The sky is softly painted.

artworks.title: Saint Euphrosyne
artworks.artist: Attributed to Melchior Steidl after Abraham Bloemaert
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with gray wash and touches of graphite, heightened with white, on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Thomas Le Claire and Katrin Bellinger
artworks.description: The image displays three figures. The central figure is seated and supported by the other two. The central figure has wavy dark hair, eyes closed, and wears a robe with a cross. The figure on the left looks serene, while the one on the right holds onto the cross. The background is sketchy with dark and light contrast, possibly depicting a dimly lit or nighttime setting with visible wooden beams.

artworks.title: Greeting Grandmother (Le Bonjour à la Grand-mère)
artworks.medium: etching with graphite additions on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image is a room sketch with three figures. In the foreground, a person lies on a bed, while another person stands near the bed, offering a child. A third individual stands by a window, holding the curtains open to let daylight in. The room includes furniture like a tall cabinet and a picture frame. The sketch is done in monochrome with shading for depth.

artworks.title: Greeting Grandmother (Le Bonjour à la Grand-mère)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, aquatint, and roulette with false-biting on Van Gelder laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image depicts three figures in a room. On the right, a person lies in bed with only their head visible, resting on a pillow. Another person stands next to the bed holding a child. The child is sitting on the person's lap, reaching towards the individual in bed. In the background to the left, a third figure is seen with arms raised, interacting with curtains or a sheet. The scene is depicted in a sketch-like, monochromatic style with detailed cross-hatching.

artworks.title: Greeting Grandmother (Le Bonjour à la Grand-mère)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, false-biting, and softground etching on Arches laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image shows a room interior containing four individuals. In the foreground, an adult is partially seen lying in bed, covered by a blanket and head resting on a pillow. This person is turned slightly on their side with one arm extended upward, reaching out towards a child. The child is held by another adult who is standing next to the bed. The child's features are small and delicate, with short hair. The adult holding them has a muscular build with short hair and facial features depicted in shadow. In the background, there is another person depicted from the back, standing near a window with light streaming through the curtains they are holding open. No explicit details of facial features can be discerned due to the shading and positioning. No visible jewelry is noted, and no objects are held by the individuals. The atmosphere of the room is characterized by a mixture of darkness and light, with the source of light coming from the window, casting the individuals in varied degrees of shadow.

artworks.title: Greeting Grandmother (Le Bonjour à la Grand-mère)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, false-biting, and softground etching on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image shows a scene with three figures in a dimly lit interior space. On the right side, there is a partially visible person reclining in a bed, seen from the waist up, with long hair cascading over the pillow. On the left, another figure stands with their back mostly to the viewer, holding an infant or small child at chest level, who appears to be reaching out or being handed to the person on the bed. To the left of them, in the background, a third figure is visible, wholly silhouetted, standing in front of a window with their arms extended holding open a curtain, creating a triangular opening of light. The room around them is mostly shadowed, creating a contrast between the brightness coming through the window and the darker, textured bedding and walls.

artworks.title: Greeting Grandmother (Le Bonjour à la Grand-mère)
artworks.medium: etching, drypoint, false-biting, softground etching, and roulette on Arches laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image shows two adults and a child in a dimly lit room. One adult, seen from behind, is standing full-length in front of a window, pulling back thick curtains to let light in. The other adult is partially visible, sitting up in bed with most of their upper body and profile shown, passively supporting a child being held by the standing adult. The child is cradled in the arms of the adult nearest them, with detail visible on a small portion of their face and body. The room is monochromatic with soft lighting, enhancing a mellow atmosphere, and features minimal furniture and textures visible beyond the individuals.

artworks.title: Sickness (La Maladie)
artworks.medium: etching and aquatint on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image depicts a scene with two individuals indoors. The first person is lying in a bed with their upper body slightly elevated against a pillow, reaching out their right hand towards the second person. The second person, standing at the foot of the bed, is extending their left arm holding a small object. The room features simple furnishings like a chair and patterned drapery on the walls. The overall lighting in the room is dim, enhancing the intimate atmosphere.

artworks.title: Misery (La Misère)
artworks.medium: etching on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image shows a person lying on their side on a bed. The person's face is partly facing upwards, with short, dark hair. They are unclothed and covered by a blanket. The room includes a bed with a blanket, a table with items on it, and a textured wall with small bottles or containers on a shelf in the background. The drawing style features cross-hatching for texture.

artworks.title: Misery (La Misère)
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint, drypoint, and printed tone on laid Van Gelder paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Bell
artworks.description: The image shows a person lying in bed, partially covered by a sheet. The person is on their side, head resting on a pillow, with eyes open. Their facial features are softly sketched, and their hair is short and slightly tousled. No specific clothing is visible due to the sheet. The room is dimly lit, with a shelf holding bottles in the background, and a shadowy stool or chair near the bed. The scene is rendered in a monochrome style with intricate hatching.
